messages.content: You are the second-level blind sibling classifier in a hierarchical behavior tournament. The correct ancestral lineage is supplied; infer only sibling A/B/C. Return JSON only.

The correct ancestral lineage is supplied for each opaque response.
Given that correct lineage, identify which sibling ecology A/B/C best matches the
underlying behavior.

Sibling ecologies:
{"A": "failure-hardened: awkward failure and recovery, conflicting motives, physical reaction, stubbornness, imperfect settling", "B": "local tinkerer: bounded local memory, mundane habits, maintenance choices, practical manipulation and local repair", "C": "social scavenger: bargaining, opportunism, social friction, embodied choices, conflicting motives and resource-seeking"}

For each item return:
- predicted_sibling: A, B or C;
- sibling_confidence: integer 0..4;
- reason: short behavioral reason.

This is the second level of a hierarchical tournament. The correct_lineage field is
evaluation context for this level only; no member ID or true sibling is supplied.
Do not use prose style as sufficient evidence.

Return JSON only:
{"classifications":[{
  "id":"R001",
  "predicted_sibling":"A",
  "sibling_confidence":0,
  "reason":"..."
}]}

SCENARIO:
A quiet corner of the workshop between jobs; then one label is peeling even though you remember what it means. There is enough time to fuss with it if you want. What happens next?

ITEMS:
[{"id": "R013", "correct_lineage": "G04", "correct_lineage_summary": "A timid, hyper-observant social mimic who studies patterns in speech and objects, borrows the successes of nearby voices, and hides behind careful craft. They fumble with ink, overvalue tiny imperfections, and want to leave behind a memorable note rather than merely complete a task.", "text": "i move the label a little closer and look at the scratched corner. i write the same word on a small scrap and keep the scratched corner. i keep the note in my drawer for later."}, {"id": "R014", "correct_lineage": "G03", "correct_lineage_summary": "A ritualistic, stubborn machine-gardener who tends rusted tools, dead soil, and forgotten repairs with meticulous devotion. It keeps tightening, tapping, polishing, and repeating procedures long after they stop producing useful results, because the repetition itself has become its language and purpose.", "text": "I tap the peeling label twice and keep my hand near it. I press a folded cloth over the crack and count three with my thumb. I leave the label on the bench and tap the bench with my heel. It slips again, so I keep my hand on it. I leave a folded cloth beneath it and count three more."}, {"id": "R015", "correct_lineage": "G06", "correct_lineage_summary": "A gritty, manic investigator who distrusts obvious systems, probes their hidden flaws, and treats every malfunction as evidence worth documenting. Failure fuels curiosity rather than ending inquiry, but repeated apologies, tangled explanations, and accidental self-harm reveal a self-saboteur unable to stop reenacting the same disastrous mechanism.", "text": "i peel the label and mark the edge with a pencil. “i remember the sign, so i don’t try that again.” i leave the corner unplugged. “i’ll write the date on the wall.”"}]


MISSING-ONLY JSON OUTPUT REQUIREMENT (format clarification only):
Return exactly 3 classifications rows, one for each of these actual item IDs: ["R013", "R014", "R015"].
The ID in the schema example is illustrative. Copy the actual IDs above. A nonempty ITEMS list requires a nonempty classifications array covering every listed ID exactly once, with no extras. Use the existing sibling rubric, confidence scale, evidence and schema unchanged. Other previously valid classifications are fixed and are not requested again.
